traits.ovary_position.note: Wikipedia Amaryllidaceae (read 2026-10-17): ~1,600 spp (APweb figure; up to ~2,260 by other counts); ovary superior in Allioideae and Agapanthoideae, inferior in Amaryllidoideae. Wikipedia Allium (read 2026-10-17): ~1,110 accepted spp, ovary superior. Allium alone is well over half the family, so superior leads.

traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA (read 2026-10-17): lamina entire, simple. German Wikipedia, Lauch (read 2026-10-17): rarely blades split into many threadlike segments.

traits.leaf_shape.note: English Wikipedia, Amaryllidaceae (read 2026-10-17): linear, strap-like, oblong, elliptic, lanceolate or threadlike; DELTA (read 2026-10-17): linear, lanceolate, oblong, ovate or orbicular; German Wikipedia, Lauch (read 2026-10-17): Allium (largest genus) flat or cylindrical, long and narrow. Weighted by Allium.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Zygomorphic Amaryllidaceae (Hippeastrum, Sprekelia) are weakly bilateral with declinate parts, not labellate. Inferred.

traits.hypanthium.note: Wikipedia Allium (read 2026-10-17): ~1,110 spp, six tepals in two whorls with no tube mentioned, ovary superior; the file's Simpson note already reads the onion subfamily as having no hypanthium and Amaryllidoideae as having a hypanthial tube. Weighted by Allium's share of the ~1,600-2,260 species (Wikipedia Amaryllidaceae), absent leads. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 385 Amaryllidaceae, which takes in the onions (tribe Allieae) and Agapanthus as APG does: herbs from a coated bulb, very rarely a rhizome; leaves few, from the base, more or less linear, with parallel veins; flowers showy, bisexual, regular, one to many in an umbel atop a leafless stalk, within two or more papery bracts; perianth of 6 petal-like parts in two whorls of 3, often with a corona; stamens 6, rarely more; ovary superior (onions) or inferior (daffodils), of three cells; fruit a capsule, or fleshy and staying shut.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, family Amaryllidaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral or distichous, usually; read as {"distichous": "often", "spiral": "often"}.

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, family Amaryllidaceae: leaf division simple, undivided; read as "simple".

traits.bract_form.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 228, family Amaryllidaceae: bract form spathe subtending flowers, usually; read as {"spathe": "usually"}.

traits.flowering_position.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, family Amaryllidaceae: flowering position terminal on a leafless scape; read as "terminal".

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, family Amaryllidaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229, family Amaryllidaceae: life span perennial; read as "perennial".

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Amaryllidaceae, with the parts of Amaryllidaceae it codes as families of their own (Alliaceae), whose further states read as sometimes: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a bulb, rarely a rhizome; with them, usually a bulb, sometimes a corm, rarely a rhizome. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add zygomorphic (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 229: actinomorphic or zygomorphic.
